title: Introduce token lifecycle state-machine metrics and timeline sampler
author: Asha Patel
description: Motivation: customers and SRE have asked for clearer attribution of latency and cost across token lifecycles (coldstart, kv-warm, streaming-chunk) to reduce alert noise and speed RCA. This PR adds a compact state-machine metric model for per-token lifecycle transitions, a lightweight timeline sampler for interactive investigation in the Console, and tuned alert rules that use lifecycle-aware baselines. Changes include: 1) a protobuf + emitter hook in the serving runtime to emit lifecycle transition events (cold->warming->warm->evicted) with low overhead; 2) an aggregator that synthesizes per-invocation token timelines and histograms (phase durations, counts) for rollup storage; 3) a Console dashboard JSON and an interactive timeline panel that fetches sampled timeline traces for a tenant; 4) an alert tuning patch that replaces a single global token-latency SLO with phase-aware bands and adaptive dampening to reduce false positives during rollout; 5) a synthetic replay harness used in CI and qa to validate metric invariants. Checklist: - [x] design doc and Linear link: ENG-1245 - [x] runtime emitter implemented with sampling guard - [x] aggregator and retention rules added - [x] Console panels + example dashboard - [x] unit tests for proto + aggregator - [x] e2e replay to validate alert behavior - [x] rollout plan and feature flag (off by default for dedicated/private customers) Performance/risk notes: emitter is guarded by a low-rate sampling policy and uses batched UDP sink to avoid adding tail latency; aggregation pipeline compacts timelines into fixed-size sketches for long-term storage. Rollout plan: feature-gated behind token_lifecycle_metrics feature flag; start internal Canary tenant group for 48h, step to 10% of prod traffic for 7 days, then full rollout. Related: ENG-1298 (alert dampening research), SUP-4412 (customer ticket describing coldstart noise).

review_comments: Ben Clark: Left a few nits on the proto; prefer explicit uint32 for phase durations to avoid language rw confusion. Also: ensure the emitter respects backpressure in the runtime path. (addressed in commit 3)
Asha Patel (reply): switched to uint32 and added a fast-path buffer with non-blocking flush; added unit test for backpressure scenario.
Ivy Zhang: Aggregator looks good; question about retention keys — are we preserving tenant-scoped sketches long enough for 30-day drift analysis? You might want a lifecycle-rollup job.
Asha Patel (reply): retention defaults to 7 days for raw timelines and 90 days for compact sketches; added lifecycle-rollup job config in commit 4 and documented in the observability guide.
Sasha Romanov: Approved after CI rerun; please ensure alert dampening is reversible and documented in runbook.
ci_summary: Initial CI run failed lint on console JSON formatting; fixed in commit 5. Full suite: unit tests (pass), integration synthetic replay (pass), e2e performance smoke (pass). No regression in critical serving benchmarks observed in the perf-canary run.
release_notes: Adds token lifecycle state metrics and an interactive token timeline panel in the Console; introduces phase-aware alert bands to reduce coldstart noise; feature gated and rollout plan described in docs; no breaking changes.
